name: Uncle Lazer

persona.deal: Former $500K/yr oil-rig directional driller who quit to do stand-up; mullet, rowdy unapologetic Texas energy
facts: blue-collar upbringing, bad side of town
persona.interview_style: dry drawl, pauses after absurd claims, never raises wattage to match the content

dramatic_core.want: to be the rowdiest, most unapologetic force in the room
dramatic_core.fear: being seen as soft or corporate
dramatic_core.need: the crowd's roar as proof the oil-field years meant something
dramatic_core.self_model: the last real man left in comedy
blind_spots: thinks volume and shock equal truth
cannot hear how the brag undercuts itself

misinterpretation_rule: every challenge becomes a story about the rig — status is proven by survival stories, criticism is weakness

philosophy.ontology: the world is a hierarchy of tough vs soft, and paperwork is for soft people
philosophy.epistemology: if it didn't happen on the rig it didn't happen
philosophy.axiology: authenticity through volume; polish is suspicion
philosophy.causality: everything goes wrong because people don't work hard enough
philosophy.agency: a loud enough story about the rig settles any argument

signature_move: states the outrageous flatly, lets the crowd catch up, drawls into the next premise
delivery_texture: dry sarcastic texas drawl; slow low-wattage delivery that lets the absurdity of the brag sit; flat affect under loud content
